core_obligations: Split off the torsion part: put M' = M[x^infinity] and use the short exact sequence 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0, which is a short exact sequence of (2,1)-periodic complexes because phi and psi preserve M', and note that M'' is x-power torsion free (proof lines 481-491).

Discard the torsion part: the three equalities e_R(M', phi, psi) = e_R(M', x phi, psi) = e_R(M' cap Im(phi), 0, x) = 0 are supplied by the comparison lemma, so additivity shows it suffices to prove the formula for (M'', phi'', psi''), reducing to the case where x acts injectively on M (proof lines 492-502).

Finish in the injective case: if x : M -> M is injective then Ker(x phi) = Ker(phi), and the displayed short exact sequence 0 -> Im(phi)/x Im(phi) -> Ker(psi)/Im(x phi) -> Ker(psi)/Im(phi) -> 0 together with the identity defining e_R proves e_R(M, x phi, psi) = e_R(M, phi, psi) - e_R(Im(phi), 0, x) (proof lines 502-509).
proof_roadmap: Separate the x-power torsion submodule and get a short exact sequence of (2,1)-periodic complexes with x-power torsion free quotient (proof lines 481-491).
Show the torsion part contributes nothing to either side, so the claim reduces to the torsion-free case (proof lines 492-502).
In the injective case compare kernels and use the displayed short exact sequence to evaluate the difference of multiplicities (proof lines 502-509).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the effect of multiplying one of the two structure maps of a (2,1)-periodic complex by an element x whose support condition dim Supp(M/xM) <= 0 forces x to behave like a parameter: e_R(M, x phi, psi) = e_R(M, phi, psi) - e_R(Im(phi), 0, x), and symmetrically for x psi (statement lines 465-475). The proof has a genuine two-stage reduction: first the x-power torsion submodule is split off and shown to contribute zero to both sides, which uses three vanishing equalities and additivity of e_R, and then in the case where x acts injectively the two kernels are compared and the difference is counted by the displayed short exact sequence ending in the identity for e_R (proof lines 481-509). The author proves only the first of the two formulas and says the second is proved in exactly the same manner; this is reproduced as written. The claim is H2.
